 Cycling
 Motorcycling-MotoGP title 'already lost' after Sepang withdrawal, says Martin
 Saturday, 31 Oct 2026
 | 1:56 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 MotoGP - Malaysian Grand Prix - Sepang International Circuit, Sepang, Malaysia - October 31, 2026 Aprilia Racing's Jorge Martin before practice REUTERS/Hasnoor Hussain 
 SEPANG, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Aprilia's Jorge ⁠Martin said on Saturday his MotoGP title challenge was effectively over ⁠after withdrawing from the Malaysian Grand Prix to continue his recovery ‌from a wrist fracture. 
 The 2024 champion pulled out before qualifying at Sepang after struggling with the injury he suffered in a sprint-race crash at Phillip Island last weekend. 
 The 28-year-old trails championship ​leader Marc Marquez by 10 points with four ⁠rounds remaining, including the Malaysian ⁠GP. 
 "I don't have to think about the championship. Maybe I can win it, ⁠but ‌for me it's already lost," Martin told reporters. 
 "For sure I will fight till the end, not only for me, because at the ⁠end of the day I'm already a champion, but for ​my team, for ‌my people, I will fight till the end, I will try again ⁠in Qatar. ​Otherwise I would stay at home and rest." 
 Martin said he had pushed to race at Sepang but lacked the strength under braking needed to compete at the highest ⁠level, prompting the decision to withdraw rather than ​risk aggravating the injury. 
 "I felt that I could ride with almost no pain, but for maybe one lap," the Spaniard said. 
 "After that I started to have a ⁠lot of pain, I couldn't be constant, so watching a bit the lap times and my performance, we decided to stop, to try to wait. 
 "We thought together with the team that the effort I was doing was too ​much to continue and nothing to gain. It was ⁠just going to be very difficult even to score one point."
 Gresini Racing's Alex ​Marquez stormed to a thrilling pole position at ‌the Malaysian MotoGP on Saturday, edging elder ​brother and reigning champion Marc Marquez, while Pedro Acosta completed the front row. 
 (Reporting by Suramya Kaushik in Bengaluru; Editing by Tom Hogue)
